title: Finite Fermat domination and genus bounds on geometric fibre components
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, $K=k(S)$, and $f:X\to S$ an H-projective morphism with $X$ integral of finite type over $k$. Assume all geometric fibres of $f$ are pure of dimension one and $C=X_K$ is smooth and geometrically integral. Put $F=k(X)$. Assume $X$ is normal. Fix a prime $\ell\geq5$ different from $\operatorname{char}k$ and assume $K$ contains a primitive $\ell$th root of unity. Let $S=\bigcup_iU_i$ be a finite affine cover and let $\varphi_i:X_{U_i}\to\mathbf P^1_{U_i}$ be finite surjective morphisms, with generic coordinate functions $x_i\in F$. Let $L/F$ and $E/K$ be finite separable field extensions embedded compatibly in $L$, such that $L$ contains elements $a_i,b_i$ with $a_i^\ell=x_i$ and $b_i^\ell=x_i-1$. Suppose the normalization of $C$ in $L$, endowed with its $E$-structure, is smooth projective geometrically integral over $E$. Put $T=\operatorname{Nor}_E(S)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Nor}_L(X)$. The structural morphism $Y\to T$ is H-projective with pure one-dimensional geometric fibres, and $Y\to X$ is finite. For each $i$, let $C_i\subset\mathbf P^2_{U_i}$ be defined by $A^\ell-B^\ell=C^\ell$, with map $\rho_i:C_i\to\mathbf P^1_{U_i}$ given by $[A:B:C]\mapsto[A^\ell:C^\ell]$. The field embedding defined by $A/C\mapsto a_i$, $B/C\mapsto b_i$ extends to a finite $U_i$-morphism
$$Y\times_SU_i\longrightarrow C_i$$
whose composite with $\rho_i$ is the given map through $X_{U_i}$. Each geometric fibre of $C_i/U_i$ is smooth geometrically integral of genus $(\ell-1)(\ell-2)/2$. For every algebraically closed field $\Omega$, geometric point $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, and reduced irreducible component $Z\subset Y_t$, choosing $i$ containing the image of $t$ gives a finite nonconstant map $Z\to(C_i)_t$, and a nonconstant map from the smooth proper normalization $Z^\nu$ to $(C_i)_t$. Consequently
$$g(Z^\nu)\geq(\ell-1)(\ell-2)/2\geq2.$$
Every $\Omega$-morphism $\mathbf P^1_\Omega\to Y_t$ is constant. More generally, for any proper finite-type $\Omega$-scheme pure of dimension one whose reduced irreducible components have normalization genus at least two, every such projective-line morphism is constant. All geometric points, including those lying over nonclosed points of $T$, are included.

Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target. A finite separable field extension is finite-dimensional with separable minimal polynomials. A finite Galois extension is a finite normal separable extension; normal for fields means that every irreducible polynomial over the smaller field with a root in the larger field splits there. For a group $G$ acting on a field $V$, $V^G$ is the subfield of elements fixed by every member of $G$. All fixed-field equalities below use the field embeddings induced by the displayed scheme maps. A primitive $\ell$th root of unity is an element of multiplicative order $\ell$. The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pure-dimension], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-fin-normalization-extension], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], [def-pc-genus], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-algebraic-closure].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-semilinear-finite-normalization-model] to $S,E/K$ with trivial group: $T$ is normal integral projective of finite type, $q:T\to S$ is finite surjective and $k(T)=E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension] at the generic point of $X$, with extension $L/F$: its normalization $Y$ is normal integral with function field $L$. Its map $\nu:Y\to X$ is finite by [lem-fin-normalization-extension-finite] and surjective by lying over [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over]. Thus $Y$ is of finite type over $k$.

proof.text:
Construct $g:Y	o T$ on normalization charts. For $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X_U$, put $R_E=\overline R^{\,E}$ and $B_L=\overline B^{\,L}$. Each element of $R_E$ satisfies a monic equation over $R\subset B$, so its specified image in $L$ belongs to $B_L$. These inclusions agree on overlaps by the localization construction [def-fin-normalization-extension], hence give $g$ with $qg=f
u$. Its generic map is $E\hookrightarrow L$, so $g$ is dominant. The map $(
u,g):Y	o X	imes_ST$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-permanence-over-separated], since its composite with the finite separated projection to $X$ is $
u$; use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] for that projection. Localization in [def-fin-normalization-extension] identifies $Y_K$ with the normalization of $C$ in $L$. As it has an $E$-structure, $Y_E=Y_K	imes_{\operatorname{Spec}E}\operatorname{Spec}E=Y_K$: equivalently localize $R_E$ at its nonzero elements. By hypothesis this generic fibre is a nonempty smooth geometrically integral curve over $E$.

All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-finite-curve-factor-projective-pure] now hold for $(S,X,T,Y,f,q,\nu,g)$: the schemes are integral of finite type, $S/k$ and $f$ are H-projective, $q$ and $\nu$ are finite surjective, the induced product map is finite, and the generic fibre of $g$ is pure of dimension one. It follows that $g$ is H-projective and every geometric fibre of $g$ is pure of dimension one. This use does not assume flatness.

A primitive root $\zeta\in K$ is regular on each $U_i$: at every point it is integral, by $\zeta^\ell=1$, and normality puts it in that local ring; these local sections are the same rational function and glue. Its order remains $\ell$ in $\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O)$, and $\ell$ is invertible since $k$ is a field of different characteristic. Thus [lem-sfb-fermat-kummer-relative-curve] applies: $C_i$ is the normalization of $P_i=\mathbf P^1_{U_i}$ in $K(x_i)(a_i,b_i)$, and its geometric fibres have the asserted smoothness, integrality and genus. The chosen roots define the stated field embedding: the generic two-root presentation of $C_i$ is a field finite over $K(x_i)$, so its unital homomorphism into $L$ is injective. To extend to $Y_i=Y\times_SU_i$, on an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset P_i$ put $\varphi_i^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)=\operatorname{Spec}B$. This is affine with $B$ finite over $A$. The integral closure of $B$ in $L$ equals that of $A$ in $L$: one inclusion uses the same monic equation, the other transitivity of integrality [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive]. The chart ring of $C_i$, being integral over $A$ inside its specified subfield of $L$, therefore maps into this common closure. The maps agree on overlaps by [def-fin-normalization-extension] and give $u_i:Y_i\to C_i$ with $\rho_i u_i=\varphi_i\nu$. The latter is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition], so $u_i$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-permanence-over-separated] applied to $\rho_i$.

proof.text: Fix any $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, and choose $i$ above its image in $S$. Write $T_i=T\times_SU_i$. The map $(u_i,g):Y_i\to C_i\times_{U_i}T_i$ is finite: its composite with the finite separated projection to $C_i$ is $u_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-permanence-over-separated]. Base change along $t$ gives a finite map $Y_t\to(C_i)_t$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]. Restrict to the reduced irreducible component $Z$ (a closed subscheme); the restriction is finite as well: a closed immersion is finite since its affine ring quotient is generated as a module by $1$, and then compose finite maps. It cannot have zero-dimensional image: if it were constant, it would be a finite surjection from $Z$ onto a point, contradicting $\dim Z=1$ and [lem-sc-finite-surjective-dimension]. More explicitly its finite closed image in the integral curve $(C_i)_t$ is either a point or the whole curve; a proper irreducible closed subset of a one-dimensional irreducible space is zero-dimensional by the definition of Krull dimension. Thus it is finite nonconstant.

$Y_t$ is proper: its H-projective embedding is a closed immersion into proper projective space [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] gives properness of the composite. Thus its closed component $Z$ is proper too. By [lem-sc-normalization-properties], $Z^
u$ is a smooth proper integral curve of dimension one: $Z$ is proper and finite type over the perfect field $\Omega$. Its composite to $(C_i)_t$ is still nonconstant since normalization is surjective. On every nonempty affine chart of $Z^
u$, geometric integrality follows from [lem-weil-pbc-algclosed-finite-type-tensor-domain] applied to its finite-type domain and any extension field of $\Omega$; the nonempty overlaps stay nonempty after field extension. Thus both curves are geometrically integral, so [lem-sfb-finite-curve-genus-monotonicity] gives $g(Z^
u)\geq g((C_i)_t)=(\ell-1)(\ell-2)/2\geq6\geq2$. This comparison includes inseparable morphisms. Every construction used the arbitrary geometric point $t$, so points above nonclosed points are included.

Prove the general last assertion. Let $W/\Omega$ be proper finite type and pure of dimension one, and $v:\mathbf P^1_\Omega	o W$ a morphism. Its irreducible image has irreducible closure contained in some irreducible component $D$ of $W$. Give $D$ its reduced structure. Since $\mathbf P^1$ is reduced, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] factors $v$ through $D$. If the image closure is a proper subset of $D$, it is a single closed point (dimension one); its residue field is $\Omega$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], and the same reduced-source factorization makes $v$ constant. Otherwise $\mathbf P^1	o D$ is dominant. The projective line is smooth and normal by [lem-asd-projective-line-genus-zero] and [lem-sc-smooth-normal], so [lem-sfb-component-dominant-normalization-lift] lifts this map to $D^
u$. By [lem-sc-normalization-properties], $D^
u$ is smooth proper integral. The same affine tensor-domain argument [lem-weil-pbc-algclosed-finite-type-tensor-domain] makes $D^
u$ geometrically integral. The lift is nonconstant because its composite is dominant onto the curve $D$. Genus monotonicity now gives $0=g(\mathbf P^1)\geq g(D^
u)\geq2$, a contradiction. Applying this result to $W=Y_t$ proves the required projective-line assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q02-d65d7e9a1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS with no fixes. The delivery adds no new nodes and does not change the item statement. It writes a 7-step proof of de Jong §3.5 (the local de Jong PDF is missing, marked WANTED; the argument was checked from memory of the paper and against Stacks curves.tex at the riemann-hurewitz section and tags 0CD0/0CD2). I checked every step against the cited statements. Step 1 gets T from the semilinear finite-normalization model with a trivial group and Y from normalization at the generic point; nu is finite and surjective by lying-over. Step 2 builds g on charts by integrality, gets (nu,g) finite by cancellation against the base change of q, and identifies the generic fibre through T x_S K = Spec E. Step 3 checks every hypothesis of finite-curve-factor-projective-pure. Step 4 shows zeta is regular because U_i is normal and l is invertible; the Fermat-Kummer node applies, A and B have the same integral closure in L by transitivity, and rho_i u_i = phi_i nu. Step 5 gets the finite map to (C_i)_t by base change, and a constant image would contradict finite-surjective-dimension. Step 6 shows Y_t is proper and Z^nu smooth and proper (normalization-properties over a perfect field), gets geometric integrality from tensor-domain, and genus monotonicity, which allows inseparable maps, gives genus at least 6. Step 7 treats the non-dominant case via a closed Omega-point and reduced-source factorization, and the dominant case via the normalization lift, which contradicts g(P1)=0. Edge cases checked: l=5, characteristic 2 or 3, inseparable maps, nonclosed base points, nonreduced or reducible fibres, E=K, empty W. No duplicates in the DAG; no SGA. The off-unit general tools (pbc normalization-in-residue-field, tensor-domain, reduced-source factorization, sc normalization properties, smooth-normal, P1 genus zero, nagata P^n proper) are accepted as tool uses. Batch-5 flag: genus-monotonicity reaches lem-trf-birational-curve-quasifinite (Stacks 0AB6, generic quasi-finiteness for dominant maps of curves). Neither the trace formula nor Poincare duality gives it and it is not a step of their proofs, so it is genuinely outside the assumptions and is not a RETURN.
